races.name: Ladies Day At Dundalk Handicap

runners_data.name: Valiant Force
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer on Standard going with a respectable sim-going record; Donagh O'Connor a capable booking and Robson De Aguiar in fair 14-day form, though a string of mid-pack finishes on turf at Goodwood suggests the return to AW is a positive switch here.

runners_data.name: The Highway Rat
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with a placed effort on Standard going in his recent history; W J Lee is a strong rider around Dundalk but 35 days off is a mild flag, and the hold-up style suits a single-pace closer role in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Howd'yadoit
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner and race-shaper by default despite a STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) indicating this is not its most natural role; Colin Keane's horsemanship gives it every chance of controlling the pace, and a win over 5f on Standard going last time out is directly relevant form.

runners_data.name: Eclairage
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type whose real running style is buried deep in the field due to redistribution — the note is that this horse's best form (2nd on Standard going) came when able to drop in and pick up late; the tp headgear and Daniel Murphy's light 14-day strike rate are mild concerns, but the AW surface is familiar.

runners_data.name: Kerdos
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up runner whose sim-going record is thin (1/15) yet the Standard surface at Dundalk is where it needs to operate; the tongue-tie (b) is already established headgear, and Jack Kearney's 3lb claim marginally offsets a modest recent form string of mostly mid-division finishes.

runners_data.name: Ipanema Queen
runners_data.note: David Egan partner with course-and-distance form including a win on Standard at Dundalk; naturally prominent and will look to press Howd'yadoit early, making her a key race-shaper — her sim-going record (1W2P from 11) is solid for this surface.

runners_data.name: Rosie Frith
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride on a three-year-old filly with a Standard-going win and a placed effort in her recent history; naturally prominent and should feature close to the pace, with course form (1W2P from 11 on sim-going) suggesting she handles this track well.

runners_data.name: Collective Power
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who is a genuine prominent-style horse but has been pushed back to midfield on the map due to congestion at the front; Chris Hayes is a shrewd pilot who may find a way forward, but the STYLE_FIT (0.92) discount and a 35-day absence after modest recent form (5-6-9 runs) lower expectations.

runners_data.name: Final Melody
runners_data.note: A mare whose entire recent form card reads 2-2-2-1-2 on Standard or near-Standard, making her one of the most consistent horses in the race on this surface; naturally prominent but mapped to midfield because there is no room — Wayne Lordan returning after a 212-day absence is the major flag, and the STYLE_FIT (0.91) underlines the positional difficulty.

runners_data.name: Fox In Flight
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old with a placed effort on Standard going and naturally prominent style that should allow Andrew Slattery to find a decent berth; sim-going record (1W4P from 10) is promising but the form string includes several disappointing runs, making reliability the question.

races.paceDynamic: Howd'yadoit is the lone confirmed front-runner and, despite a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting this is slightly out of its natural role, Colin Keane should press it to the front immediately on this 5f Dundalk AW track, setting a sustainable rather than scorching pace with minimal pressure from behind. The prominent runners — Ipanema Queen, Rosie Frith, and Fox In Flight — will fight for the close-up positions directly behind, while Final Melody and Collective Power, both true prominent types redistributed to midfield, will be unable to secure their natural berths in a field this compressed. The hold-up horses Valiant Force, The Highway Rat, Kerdos, and Eclairage (a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield) will be rearward and face a straightforward sprint home with no bends to navigate. This race shape — one genuine front-runner, a contested prominent band, and a clean gallop on a flat AW track — strongly favours hold-up horses with a high cruising speed who can produce one late run into a weakening lead, making true closers and horses with proven Standard-going form the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Howd'yadoit Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Howd'yadoit leads uncontested at a fair pace and the prominent pack cannot close the gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Keane dictates from the front without being seriously pressed, meaning the race develops into a test of who can sustain their finishing effort over the last two furlongs; hold-up horses need a strong enough gallop to reel in the leader, and any that fire their run early may fall short.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Overrun Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Ipanema Queen or Rosie Frith push up aggressively and turn the race into a burn-up that swamps Howd'yadoit before the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A contested pace sees the field string out quickly and stamina becomes the deciding factor over the final 1f; prominent-style horses who settle just behind the pace and quicken cleanly benefit most, while those who raced too keenly will empty.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late charge, giving hold-up horses a clear target to aim at in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Valiant Force or The Highway Rat, both carrying Standard-going form, produce a sustained late run as the prominent horses fade; the flat Dundalk track with no final bend suits a straight closing burst and this scenario rewards horses who have been saved for one effort.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Midfield Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Final Melody or Collective Power manage to grab a better position than their mapped slot suggests and rally from a handy pitch.
scenarios.body: Both are genuine prominent types squeezed back by the numbers, but if the pace fragments and gaps appear mid-race, one could find a clear run and produce a competitive finish; their STYLE_FIT discounts make this a low-probability but non-zero outcome.

watchPoints.text: Howd'yadoit (Keane) and Ipanema Queen (Egan) — watch the first 2 furlongs closely to see whether Keane is challenged for the lead; if Egan pushes Queen up hard, the pace will be materially faster and the race shape flips from controlled to contested, dramatically changing the scenario probabilities.

Final Melody has a 212-day absence after a career built entirely on placed efforts at Standard going — if she returns forward and bounces straight back to form under Lordan, the redistribution label may understate her chance, but fitness is unproven.

Collective Power and Final Melody both being genuine prominent types forced back in the field creates a mid-race bunching risk — horses immediately behind the pace could face a wall of traffic at the 2f pole if any of those horses push forward unexpectedly.

Eclairage (tp, James Ryan) posted a 2nd on Standard going in recent history and is a true hold-up horse whose natural finishing run could be masked by its midfield map position — watch whether Ryan drops it out early and threads through, signalling it is running to its actual style rather than its mapped one.

Rosie Frith has back-to-back placed efforts at Dundalk on Standard (1W2P) and Dylan Browne McMonagle is in strong form — if Howd'yadoit sets only a moderate pace, she is best placed of the prominent types to sustain a challenge through the final furlong.

races.name: RACING TV FREE ONE MONTH TRIAL Handicap

runners_data.name: Reimagined
runners_data.note: Ben Coen on a hold-up three-year-old who has a pattern of fading in the finish; all five recent runs came over shorter (5f-6f) on turf, so the step to 7f on polytrack is an untested combination and there is a genuine distance concern here.

runners_data.name: Wild Berries
runners_data.note: Siobhan Rutledge partnered hold-up type who has run well over 7f on good turf (6/7f/GOO) but has been off 39 days and the Ross O'Sullivan yard is 0/10 in the 14-day window — the combination of a quiet trainer and a fading-in-finish flag makes her tough to place positively.

runners_data.name: Iff In Doubt
runners_data.note: Dundalk course winner over 7f (1/7f/STA) and runner-up over 8f here — the track form is strong; W J Lee rides and the headgear (t) is retained; a natural hold-up horse whose true closer's role is squeezed by the overcrowded rear, so expect a midfield berth rather than last, which slightly blunts his finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Kc Bear
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over on this progressive three-year-old who has hit the frame five times in five starts including a course win over 6f and placed twice at 7f-8f on Dundalk; prominent style suits this shape perfectly and the Noel Meade yard is 2/12 in the 14-day period.

runners_data.name: Gonna Be Golden
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter who has won over this exact course and distance (1/7f/STA); headgear (t) worn, trainer Oliver 1/8 in the 14-day window, but STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) acknowledges she is being relied upon to lead here — if she does, she controls the race; her four subsequent runs since that win have been disappointing and consistency is the question.

runners_data.name: Sagasti
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over on a horse with a placed effort at 7f on this surface (3/7f/STA); wears visor (v) for the first time, which can sharpen early focus; hold-up style makes him reliant on a strong pace that may not materialise here, and the visor adds an unknown element.

runners_data.name: Fate's Gambit
runners_data.note: Consistent horse whose five-run string shows all finishes between 3rd and 5th, with one placed effort on this surface; Robson De Aguiar yard is 0/4 in 14 days but the horse's prominent style slots in neatly behind the leader and he rarely runs a bad race.

runners_data.name: Whistling Jamesie
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on this surface (1/6f/STA) but has been off 39 days and carries the fades-in-finish warning; Wayne Lordan rides but the horse's natural hold-up style is displaced to midfield by the overcrowded rear, meaning he will likely race closer than ideal and may burn energy earlier than suits him, blunting the finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Mountain Memory
runners_data.note: Unpredictable runner (style U) with only three career runs on record; Andrew Slattery trains and rides, which is a rare combination at this level; the fading-in-finish flag and small sample of form make him the most unknown quantity in the race, and 15 days since last run is straightforward.

runners_data.name: Bullet Bourbon
runners_data.note: Low-rated (OR 52) hold-up type who finished 2nd on this surface over 6f (2/6f/STA) and has shown some ability but consistency is poor; Robert Whearty rides and, with only 10 days since last run, fitness is not the concern — rather, the horse tends to fade and is genuinely squeezed out of his natural position by the busy rear of the field.

runners_data.name: Push Harder
runners_data.note: Steps down from 8f to 7f for Chris Timmons (trainer-jockey combination) and has placed at 8f on this surface (3/8f/STA); headgear (ht) — hood and tongue-tie — retained; lowest OR in the field at 44 and, as a natural hold-up type repositioned into midfield, faces the steepest ask if the pace does not draw out runners in front.

races.paceDynamic: Gonna Be Golden is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no natural rival to pressure her from the gates, she can dictate a sustainable, metronomic gallop on the Dundalk polytrack over seven furlongs. Behind her, Kc Bear and Fate's Gambit are likely to track prominently, creating a compact lead group but no genuine pace war. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Whistling Jamesie, Iff In Doubt, Bullet Bourbon and Push Harder are genuine closers by nature but are mapped into midfield because the rear is overcrowded, meaning several will race closer to the pace than is natural for them, compressing the field and reducing the gap the true hold-up horses must bridge. A sustainable, uncontested gallop over seven furlongs at Dundalk strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and pick up in the straight — the leader controls tempo, the finish is set up for the front-rank and prominent profiles rather than pure closers bursting from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gonna Be Golden Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Gonna Be Golden secures the lead uncontested and sets a fair but controlled pace throughout.
scenarios.body: She travels within herself for six furlongs before Sam Coen (5) kicks in the straight, and a tempo-controlled race rewards the front-running profile with fitness and tactical control.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Gonna Be Golden is reeled in late by Kc Bear or Fate's Gambit after sitting just off the pace.
scenarios.body: The steady gallop allows Kc Bear or Fate's Gambit to track the leader on the bridle and pounce inside the final furlong without expending energy in a tactical fight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runner Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that a sharp, progressive horse from the midfield pack can close the gap on the turn.
scenarios.body: Iff In Doubt, with proven form at Dundalk over this trip including a win at the track, is best placed of the displaced hold-up types to deliver a late challenge if the field concertinas.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upsets the Shape
scenarios.trigger: If disrupted early pace or wide draws fracture the field and allow a low-rated improver to steal through on the rail.
scenarios.body: Mountain Memory or Bullet Bourbon benefits from a chaotic scenario where pace and positional order break down entirely, though their form and ratings make this a low-probability route to the frame.

watchPoints.text: Gonna Be Golden's early supremacy is the hinge of this race — watch whether Sam Coen (5) allows her to stride on cleanly from the gates or gets crowded wide by Kc Bear and Fate's Gambit, because any significant pressure on her in the first two furlongs transforms the entire tempo calculation.

Iff In Doubt and Whistling Jamesie are true closers who will be forced to race in midfield — if the pace is slow, they will be trapped in a pocket with nowhere to go on the home turn and may find themselves unable to produce their natural finish.

Sagasti wears a visor for the first time — first-time headgear can produce an improved or erratic early response, and if he jumps sharply and takes a prominent position it could disrupt the order behind Gonna Be Golden in the early stages.

Kc Bear's draw and Colin Keane's positioning in the first furlong are worth noting — if Keane slots directly behind the leader without cover, Kc Bear is the horse most likely to produce the winning challenge in Scenario B.

The 39-day breaks for both Wild Berries and Whistling Jamesie are notable in a race where most rivals are race-fit; watch how both travel early and whether they drop out tamely from the two-furlong pole, which would confirm the fitness angle.

races.name: Anglo Printers - Award Winning Print And Packaging Maiden
QuinnBet Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Kitty Bear
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner and form horse; won over this trip at Goodwood and at 7f on Soft, and trainer Slattery fires 4 from 32 in 14 days, suggesting this is a live run — the key question is whether she can convert control into victory on Standard AW, a surface on which she showed pace last time (9 days ago).|

runners_data.name: Navajo Point
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has faded in the finish in recent starts and whose last five runs are all placed ninth or worse at 7-9f on Good; nothing in the record here suggests he can land a blow from off the pace on this surface.|

runners_data.name: Famous Enough
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who placed second over 8f on Standard AW, the closest statistical match to today; trainer Foley has not fired one from seven in 14 days and the tongue-tie is retained, but the course-and-distance form gives him a clear tactical foothold.|

runners_data.name: Micasso
runners_data.note: Won last time over 8f on Good and brings genuine quality, but his natural style is a true hold-up run from the rear — he has been displaced to midfield on this map because the field is saturated with backmarkers, meaning he is unlikely to get his preferred position and the style-fit discount is material here.|

runners_data.name: Akashaa
runners_data.note: Another genuine hold-up type whose last two placed efforts came over this trip on Standard, yet the crowded hold-up section of this field means he will struggle to settle where he wants; Chris Hayes is the booking upgrade but the positional compromise is the limiting factor.|

runners_data.name: Movin And Groovin
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 429 days off; showed three placed efforts on Standard AW previously but the long absence is a significant concern, and Marnane has not sent one out in 14 days in this spell — treat the fitness question as the headline.|

runners_data.name: Bella Colombia
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field (60) and a dual winner, including over 8f on Standard; W J Lee takes the ride which is a strong booking, and her hold-up style should find a clear run late in a compressed race — the fade flag is absent here and the form figures on this surface (1 win, 2 places from 6) are the best in the race.|

runners_data.name: Captain Ciano
runners_data.note: Has faded in the finish repeatedly, with form figures of 0,0,0,9,8 in recent starts and no win or place from four runs on Good or Standard at distances of 8-10f; the style and form combine unfavourably here.|

runners_data.name: Angel Of Promise
runners_data.note: Carry a fade flag and all five recent runs were at 6-7f, shorter than today's mile; the step up in trip looks the chief concern, visor retained, and the form figures on Good are deep — this is an awkward fit.|

runners_data.name: Rockbury Lad
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type (7yo) who fades in the finish and whose best recent effort here was sixth from ten; tongue-tie retained, Colin Keane is an elite booking but the record suggests the horse finds a reason not to win rather than a gear he's not shown.|

runners_data.name: Fleetfootsoldier
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins from six on Standard AW and second over 7f on this surface; the 24-day freshener may suit a 6yo who tailed off ninth last time, and the tongue-tie is in play — this is a yard (Burns) that runs few and this entry stands out.|

runners_data.name: Rampage
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type who has not won or placed at the level in recent starts; displaced to midfield on the map but is a true backmarker, and the style-fit compromise makes it hard to see him delivering here despite the track specialist profile (multiple Standard AW runs).|

runners_data.name: My Vonnie
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who has run six consecutive races at distances of 8-12f on Standard and failed to win any, with best effort a sixth; returning from 128 days off is the other concern, and the style redistribution means she will not get her natural position in a crowded rear section.|

runners_data.name: Cosmic Force
runners_data.note: Has run eleven times on Standard AW — the most of any runner — and placed twice, but never won and form figures show consistent mid-pack finishes at 6-8f; a true hold-up type pushed into midfield, and the OR of 42 reflects his current level.|

runners_data.name: Monroe Dasher
runners_data.note: Fade flag applies, has run zero from five recently with a unseated rider in the string, and the form figures at 7-9f on Good are uniformly in double figures; no jockey listed in the racecard data is an additional flag — treat as a significant outsider.|

runners_data.name: Roman Harry
runners_data.note: Has won once from eight on Standard (3f placed from 8) and the trainer Duffy fires 1 from 2 in 14 days; a natural backmarker placed into midfield by the crowded hold-up section — if he gets a clear run he has placed three times at this distance and surface, but the positional compromise is real.|

runners_data.name: Desert Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Has three placed efforts from six on Standard AW over 7-8f and carries headgear (p); a true hold-up type who cannot get his natural position today, and the OR of 40 is the joint-lowest in the field — the form figures of 2,3 at this distance give a glimmer but the style redistribution and low class ceiling cap expectations.|

races.paceDynamic: Kitty Bear is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and is expected to coast into a position on or near the lead from stall, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop on Standard Dundalk AW. With no genuine pace rival to pressurise her, she can dictate terms through the first half of the mile and control the tempo into the home straight. The field behind is dominated by hold-up and prominent types — Bella Colombia, Rockbury Lad, Angel Of Promise, Captain Ciano, Navajo Point and others all want to race off the pace, meaning the midfield will be congested and those tracking Kitty Bear from close proximity (Famous Enough, Fleetfootsoldier, Movin And Groovin) are best placed to strike. The field holds materially more hold-up horses than can be placed naturally at the rear, with Roman Harry, Micasso, Akashaa, Rampage, My Vonnie, Cosmic Force, Monroe Dasher and Desert Of The Sea all redistributed to midfield — of these, Roman Harry and Micasso are most likely to actually secure a competitive midfield berth given their recent form and jockey bookings. The race shape strongly favours hold-up or prominent runners who can slot in just behind Kitty Bear and produce a clean run in the straight, as the modest pace will compress the field and closers off a slow gallop will face a punishing late sprint against a horse who has already controlled the race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Kitty Bear is allowed to coast at a controlled tempo and no prominent rival has the gate speed to push her.
scenarios.body: Kitty Bear dictates a modest fractions-based gallop throughout, making all from a handy draw, and those tracking her closely enough to pounce lack the acceleration to reel her in when she kicks for home; her recent Goodwood win over this course type and distance confirms she can go all the way at a sustainable tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Outsprint Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate enough that Famous Enough or Fleetfootsoldier track Kitty Bear in second or third and quicken past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With no pressure on the leader through the middle portion, the race becomes a sprint from the two-furlong pole, favouring those who have raced prominently and have a clean passage; Famous Enough's second on Standard AW here and Fleetfootsoldier's strong surface record make them the chief threats in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Cuts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the slow pace causes the field to bunch entirely and a midfield runner gets a clean run to the outside turning in.
scenarios.body: Bella Colombia, who won on Standard AW and handles this trip well, or Akashaa, who placed twice at this distance, could benefit if a gap opens and they produce a late surge in a race where traffic is the chief risk given the size of the field; however, true hold-up types like Akashaa are racing out of their natural position, reducing the reliability of this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unexpectedly stronger than forecast and front-end horses fade, opening the race for backmarkers.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on redistributed hold-up horses — Micasso, Roman Harry — getting their true running style right at the back, which is unlikely given the congestion in the field and the modest expected tempo; even if they find clear air late, a slow gallop rarely generates enough tempo for true closers to pick up ground from off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Kitty Bear is the only confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field — if she breaks cleanly and no prominent rival has the speed to go with her, she could be left alone to dictate a falsely slow pace that turns the race into a sprint for second.

The midfield section is dangerously congested with eight redistributed hold-up horses all forced closer than ideal — watch for a significant traffic risk in the home straight as true backmarkers try to find gaps in a compressed field.

Bella Colombia holds the joint-top OR and the best record on Standard AW in the field; if W J Lee can get a clean passage from mid-division, she represents the biggest threat to any front-end winner and should be tracked throughout the straight.

Movin And Groovin returns from 429 days off — if the prominent racer shows rustiness in the early stages and drops out of contention, the pace picture becomes even thinner and the solo lead for Kitty Bear is more pronounced.

Famous Enough wears a tongue-tie and has the clearest course-and-distance placed form on Standard; monitor how quickly he travels in the first half-mile — if he is second or third early, he becomes the most likely challenge to Kitty Bear's control.|

races.name: Fairways Hotel Dundalk Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Celtic Druid
runners_data.note: Won twice on this surface over shorter (12f STA) and steps up in trip here; sole front-runner with a clear lead by default, though a 1m4f trip on a Standard surface against multiple prominent types is a test of stamina — style fit of 0.91 reflects slight positional awkwardness for a horse shown as prominent rather than lead.|

runners_data.name: Dancing Steve
runners_data.note: Beaten a combined 43+ lengths across last five starts including at this track, headgear visor fitted but no obvious signs of recovery; true hold-up style suits a strong pace that simply isn't forecast here, and sim-going record of 0 wins from 4 placings on Standard underlines a modest profile.|

runners_data.name: Baila Conmigo
runners_data.note: A genuine closer by nature — though mapped to midfield given the density of hold-up types — who has won on Standard and placed at 16f on Good, so trip and surface are fine; 42 days since last run is worth noting, but Ciaran Murphy runners can reappear fresh, and a style-fit caveat of 0.93 should temper expectations given they cannot settle as far back as ideal.|

runners_data.name: Rich Belief
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old fitted with tongue-tie and bar who hasn't run in 78 days (33 days for jockey); best form at extended trips (17f, 18f), making this 14f a potentially short enough test, and no Standard going form among recent runs.|

runners_data.name: Porsche Lad
runners_data.note: Fitted with a blinker and has placed twice at 7f STA; coming back from 9 days ago and handles Standard well with a sim-going record of 2W8P — a prominent racer who should find a clean passage in second or third and is well-suited to a steady gallop on this surface.|

runners_data.name: Tero D'rosa
runners_data.note: Won at 10f Good and placed at 10f STA for a yard in strong current form (4 wins from 20 in 14 days); stepping up from a mile-plus trip, and sim-going record on Standard is thin (0W2P), but prominent style is naturally advantaged in this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Chopsticks
runners_data.note: Has placed at 12f STA and wears a hood; trainer McConnell quiet (0/22 in 14 days) and recent form includes a third on this surface which is the key positive — prominent style suits the pace map perfectly, though trip looks towards the upper end of their comfort zone.|

runners_data.name: Rising Sky
runners_data.note: Blinkers and tongue-tie fitted; won at 11f Good but all five recent runs on Good ground, no Standard form on record, making the surface switch a genuine unknown — prominent style is fine for this shape but the going query tempers confidence.|

runners_data.name: Grey Fable
runners_data.note: Won at 12f STA last time for Thornton, giving him two in-form runners in this race; a natural hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map position by field congestion, so the style-fit tag (0.92) is relevant — however, proven winning form on Standard at a similar trip is the strongest going credential in the field.|

runners_data.name: Sutton Hoo
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner (OR 71) and won at 10f STA last time; unexposed 3-year-old who is lightly raced and steps up in trip — hold-up style means they need luck in running but the class edge and sim-going win from just 4 runs is eye-catching.|

runners_data.name: Sonny Corleone
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott 3-year-old (5 winners from 46 in 14 days) who has placed twice at 10f STA; hold-up style means they need the pace to set up properly — on only three career runs this horse is inexperienced at this trip and likely needs things to fall right.|

runners_data.name: Mystic Rose
runners_data.note: Lowest OR in the field (50) and fitted with tongue-tie and hood; mapped to midfield from a true hold-up position because the map is full at the rear, and a style-fit of 0.90 compounds the concern — no Standard going form in recent history and best position of 4th in last five runs.|

runners_data.name: Folk Warrior
runners_data.note: Lowest weight (119lbs) and a natural closer whose trainer has no runners in the 14-day window; sim-going shows 0 wins from 1 run on Standard, all recent form on Good or Soft, and being pushed out of the natural hold-up spot by redistribution (style-fit 0.90) makes this a difficult race to win from their likely position.|

races.paceDynamic: Celtic Druid is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival looking to take them on for the lead, they should coast into an uncontested position and set a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m4f Dundalk AW trip. Porsche Lad, Tero D'rosa, Chopsticks, and Rising Sky will all press for prominent positions just behind, meaning the early sections will involve jostling for berths in the first five but without materially lifting the tempo. The result is a race likely run at an even, unhurried pace that favours those able to travel close to the action and produce a turn-of-foot in the straight, rather than those needing a genuine end-to-end test to make ground from the rear. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and tracked-pace horses who can sit second or third and pounce, with true hold-up horses at a structural disadvantage given the moderate gallop. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Baila Conmigo, Grey Fable, Mystic Rose, and Folk Warrior are all natural closers but are redistributed to midfield on the map; of these, Baila Conmigo and Grey Fable have the profile to make the best of an imperfect position given their course and distance form.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Celtic Druid Controls Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Celtic Druid escapes pressure and dictates a steady, uncontested gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Celtic Druid sets fractions to suit themselves and the race becomes a test of who can travel economically and quicken in the straight; a prominent or tracked position will be decisive. Horses sitting second to fourth with pace in hand — particularly those with Dundalk Standard form — are best placed to pounce on the long run to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Produces Winner
scenarios.trigger: If Celtic Druid fades in the straight and one of the pressing group sustains their effort to the line.
scenarios.body: With multiple horses contesting the prominent spots, a strong-finishing prominent racer who travels within themselves and quickens late will overhaul a fading leader. Sutton Hoo or Baila Conmigo, both capable of running on from just off the pace, could take advantage if the complexion opens up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and a clear gap materialises for a closer.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up horse would need the field to bunch and then split to thread through, a rare but possible outcome in a large field on a turning track. Grey Fable or Sonny Corleone would be the primary beneficiaries given their profiles, but this scenario is discounted because most of the genuine hold-up types are not in their natural positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so slow that the race degenerates into a sprint finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: An unusually slow early tempo compresses the field and turns the contest into a speed test, where horses with lower weights and those able to quicken sharply at short notice have an edge. Rising Sky and Chopsticks, both with prominent profiles and decent Dundalk handicap form, could thrive in a bunched finish, though this outcome is unlikely given the number of prominent types ensuring at least a working gallop.

watchPoints.text: Celtic Druid's ability to control fractions unchallenged is the single most important factor — if Porsche Lad or Rising Sky push up aggressively early, the tempo lifts and the shape shifts dramatically toward hold-up horses.|
Grey Fable won last time on this surface at 12f STA and is trained by the same yard as Rich Belief — watch for a dual runner scenario where one leads the hold-up challenge if a gap appears late.|

Sutton Hoo is a top-rated but unexposed 3-year-old stepping into 1m4f for the first time; if the trip suits, the OR advantage could prove decisive, but jockey Paddy Harnett will need to position them closer than their usual hold-up role dictates.|

Baila Conmigo's 42-day absence and natural hold-up style, combined with the redistribution to midfield, means watch their early positioning — if they get a clean run into second or third the style-fit concern diminishes sharply.|
Tero D'rosa's trainer Ross O'Sullivan has 4 winners from 20 runners in the last 14 days — a live yard angle in a race where prominent runners are structurally favoured by the pace map.|

races.name: Border Boutique Hire Maiden

runners_data.name: Dorie Miller
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner on OR=120 but carries a credible fade-in-finish flag backed by form figures showing consistent late-race capitulation; 36-day break and heavy weight of 145lbs compound concerns, and a hold-up style in a steady-paced race is a structural mismatch.

runners_data.name: Let's Smash It
runners_data.note: Returning from 219 days off and racing over the longest trip of its short career so far; holds the front-running role naturally but the lengthy absence and youth (2yo) raise serious stamina and fitness questions, though the controlled pace it will set plays to its strengths if it stays the trip.

runners_data.name: Matties Point
runners_data.note: Entirely unknown quantity — lightly raced with going listed as UNKNOWN and no public form to parse; W J Lee is a top booking for a horse with potential, and W McCreery's single strike from 14 over the period tempers stable expectations, but the blank slate cuts both ways.

runners_data.name: Police Gazette
runners_data.note: Holds genuine course form (3rd at Dundalk over 12f on Standard) and has a 2-from-2 record on sim-going; the hold-up tag is authentic but the lack of a strong pace to close into remains the tactical obstacle, and 47 days since last run is unremarkable.

runners_data.name: Reynir
runners_data.note: Has the clearest profile fit for this race shape — a genuine prominent runner with solid form figures (5-3-2) on good-to-soft going over 10f, now stepping up in trip which should suit; Ben Coen is a strong booking and JP Murtagh's yard has been active (4/36 T14) suggesting the horse is ready.

runners_data.name: Perggosa
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by nature, though the crowded rear forces a midfield mapping here; OR=42 and a form string of 0-099 on varying surfaces makes its chance marginal regardless of position, and the fade-in-finish warning suggests it rarely picks up meaningfully when it matters.

races.paceDynamic: Let's Smash It is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner maiden over 1m2½f at Dundalk, and with just one horse intent on leading, the pace is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than pressured. Reynir, a genuine prominent type, will push forward to track Let's Smash It, meaning the early gallop is not entirely uncontested but is unlikely to be truly searching. The hold-up brigade of Dorie Miller, Police Gazette, and the redistributed Perggosa will be forced to settle further back than ideal, though Perggosa's placement in midfield on this map is a function of overcrowding at the rear rather than a natural preference for that position. This race shape — a steady, single-paced gallop set by one front-runner with a small field — strongly favours prominent racers and resolute stayers who travel close to the pace and can pick off a tying leader in the closing stages; hold-up horses are structurally disadvantaged by the lack of pace injection to close into. The field holds more hold-up types than can all occupy the rear advantageously, with Perggosa the one most likely displaced from its natural role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady gallop, prominent wins
scenarios.trigger: If Let's Smash It dictates an honest but untroubled pace and the race lacks a meaningful surge to close into.
scenarios.body: Let's Smash It controls from the front on a comfortable lead, with Reynir the closest pursuer; the steady tempo rewards those racing within themselves near the pace from the outset.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader stops, chaser pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Let's Smash It's long absence (219 days) tells late and the horse ties up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Reynir, having tracked throughout and conserved energy in a controlled race, finds the most to give inside the final two furlongs as the leader weakens; prominence throughout pays off.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse rattles through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and the closers get a target to chase.
scenarios.body: Police Gazette, with course form and experience over the trip, would be best placed of the genuine hold-up types to pick up late; Dorie Miller has the class on OR but carries a fade-in-finish flag that limits confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank outsider gate-crashes
scenarios.trigger: If the unknown quantity Matties Point (lightly raced, going unknown, debut marker) shows unexposed ability to outclass this field.
scenarios.body: With W J Lee aboard and trainer W McCreery recording a live entry, Matties Point could benefit from an honest pace that exposes opponents' limitations; the wide-open unknown profile is the sole appeal here.

watchPoints.text: Let's Smash It's 219-day absence is the key variable — if it shows any sign of race-rustiness or stamina failure rounding the final bend, the entire race shape unravels as Reynir inherits a clear advantage.

Perggosa is a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield by necessity, not preference — watch whether Rory Cleary attempts to push it forward early; if so, it may race against its natural instincts and tire badly.

Dorie Miller's fade-in-finish flag combined with 145lbs weight and a hold-up style in a likely slow-run race creates a compounding risk — monitor whether it can even get competitive in the final furlong rather than fading as the form suggests.

Matties Point is wholly unexposed and debuts in an OR=120 field despite having no public rating benchmark — an eye-catching move by connections if the horse is live, making it a horse to track in the betting market before the off.

With all six runners on Standard going at Dundalk and the previous 4:20 race also run at Standard, track conditions are entirely predictable — no going-based shocks expected, meaning form assessment and positioning are the dominant factors today.

races.name: Family Funday At Dundalk Saturday 15th August Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Annacroft
runners_data.note: Holds the joint-highest OR in the race at 120 and has placed at 12f and 13f recently, suggesting the trip is suitable, but the ⚠ fade flag is a concern on a track where the straight rewards sustained finishing — Robert Whearty rides and trainer McConnell has 3 wins from 22 runners in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Duvessa
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's filly is the sole confirmed front-runner and Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride; she has form at 12f and 13f in soft conditions, stepping onto a Standard AW surface here, and her confirmed lead role means she will get an uncontested lead which is a substantial tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Forthill
runners_data.note: P Twomey sends her out on a 92-day absence, which is the longest layoff in the field, but her three recent runs all come at 11–12f and she has placed twice at the trip; W J Lee is a reliable rider and she is the most natural horse to press Duvessa from a prominent berth.

runners_data.name: Rocket Robyn
runners_data.note: Martin Hassett's filly has struggled for form recently with a sequence of deep finishes (9-8-0-6-9), and while she wears a tongue-tie (hg:t), her true nature as a hold-up horse means she has been placed into a midfield slot on the map that overstates her likely early position — a slow pace will do her no favours.

runners_data.name: Tequila
runners_data.note: David Egan takes the ride on a filly returning from 290 days off the track, which is a significant fitness question mark; her similar-going record reads 2 runs, 0 wins, 0 places, and her natural closing instinct is suppressed in a map that places her in midfield only because the field is backloader-heavy — treat the shown position with caution.

runners_data.name: Wheres The Gold
runners_data.note: Robert Whearty rides a filly whose OR of 120 flatters a recent form string of near-zeros (00/007); the tongue-tie (hg:p) is applied, possibly to sharpen her focus, but trainer Paul W Flynn has just 1 win from 13 recent runners and there is little to suggest she can reverse her current downward trajectory.

races.paceDynamic: Duvessa is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no genuine rival for the lead, she will likely dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m2½f trip on Standard Dundalk AW. Forthill may press from a prominent position, but with Duvessa's connections unlikely to be troubled for the early lead, the pace will be modest and metronomic rather than contested. Annacroft, Wheres The Gold, and the redistributed Tequila and Rocket Robyn will be ridden from behind, but the latter two are true hold-up types pushed into a midfield mapping only because the field contains more deep-closers than can all naturally sit at the rear — Duvessa and Forthill are the horses most likely to actually secure the positions they need. A steady pace set by Duvessa strongly favours horses who can race prominently or track the leader into the straight and quicken from a position of comfort, rather than genuine late closers trying to make up ground from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Duvessa Controls And Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Duvessa leads uncontested and converts her prominent position into a race-long advantage at a steady tempo.
scenarios.body: Duvessa dictates the fractions from the front without any rival willing or able to challenge her for the lead, leaving her poised to quicken clear once asked in the straight; a slow-to-moderate gallop plays directly into her hands and allows her to conserve energy at the head of affairs. Forthill, tracking in second, is the main beneficiary if Duvessa weakens late, having held prominent positions in recent runs and likely getting a position right behind the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Duvessa sets a true steady pace and Forthill or Annacroft tracks close enough to overhaul her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A controlled gallop means the race is not truly won until the straight, and a horse sitting close to Duvessa throughout the race will have the energy reserves to mount a meaningful challenge; Forthill's recent form shows she is capable of placing off this kind of pace at this trip on soft ground, and a firmer AW surface could bring out more speed. Annacroft drops back in distance but her hold-up profile means she needs others to do the donkey work — if the pace is genuinely slow she may find herself closer than usual.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace surprisingly collapses in the straight, opening a window for Tequila or Rocket Robyn to sweep through from behind.
scenarios.body: Tequila returns from a 290-day break and, while her redistribution to midfield reflects more hold-up horses in the field than the map accommodates, her natural instinct is to come from off the pace — if the race falls apart in the straight she could benefit; similarly, Rocket Robyn's redistribution conceals a true hold-up profile, and a bunched late finish could flatter her. Both however carry STYLE_FIT discounts and the slow-pace scenario makes their ground-making task harder rather than easier, constraining this scenario's likelihood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Shock
scenarios.trigger: If form lines prove unreliable and Wheres The Gold, who has shown modest form, runs well above her recent placings.
scenarios.body: Wheres The Gold carries the joint-highest OR (120) in the field but has a poor recent string of zeros, and a tongue-tie in headgear (hg:p) may help; a very steady pace that compresses the field could theoretically allow her to be competitive late but her history of finishing well down the field makes this a long-shot scenario. Without a compelling pace angle in her favour and with fading form, this outcome depends on a significant step up from recent efforts.

watchPoints.text: Duvessa leads alone — watch whether Dylan Browne McMonagle sets a truly crawling gallop that gifts her an uncontested procession, as this scenario makes her very hard to beat at any price.
Forthill returns from 92 days off and W J Lee may need to manage her freshness; if she overraces early chasing Duvessa rather than settling in second, she may not last home at 1m2½f on an AW surface.

Tequila has been off for 290 days and David Egan will likely ride her conservatively — watch the betting market for any market move that suggests stable confidence despite the layoff, as it would upgrade her chance significantly.

Both Rocket Robyn and Tequila are true hold-up horses mapped to midfield due to field composition — if either breaks smartly and ends up closer to the pace than expected, their redistribution tag should be revisited and their scenario probability revised upward.

Wheres The Gold and Annacroft both carry the ⚠ fade flag — if the pace is genuinely slow and the race bunches in the straight, watch whether either can avoid their habitual late weakening on this occasion.
